title: Development of capitalism
competency: List the main features of capitalism and describe the theoretical foundations of Marxian economics.

keywords.def: An economic system of private ownership of the means of production, run for profit in free markets.

Book: buying goods at one price and selling higher for profit. Fuller meaning: the 16th–18th century state policy of gaining wealth (gold, silver) through more exports than imports, colonies and regulation.
"Leave alone": markets should work without government intervention.
Karl Marx's ideas, the opposite of capitalism: collective or state ownership and central planning.

en.text: Capitalism grew out of decaying feudalism and was fully fledged in Britain and the Netherlands in the 16th–17th centuries, the age of mercantilism. Protestant ethics and strong nation states helped it. In the 18th century Adam Smith and others attacked mercantilism, and from the mid-18th century industrial capitalism arose as merchant capital was invested in machinery.

screens.title: Mercantilism and after
paras: The book defines mercantilism as buying goods and selling them higher for profit.
More fully, it was a state policy of the 16th–18th centuries.
States tried to gain gold and silver by exporting more than they imported.
Mercantilists believed world wealth was fixed.
So one state could gain only if another lost.
In the 18th century Adam Smith and others attacked these ideas.
Industrial capitalism then arose in the mid-18th century.
Capital built up by merchants was invested in machinery.

ideas.name: Features of capitalism and Adam Smith

en.text: Capitalism has five main features: private ownership of the means of production, a split between capitalists and wage workers, reinvestment of capital to enlarge production, the profit motive, and laissez-faire, markets free of government intervention. Adam Smith (1723–1790), a Scottish economist, set out this classical idea in "The Wealth of Nations" (1776).

opts: The government takes all of it
Nobody; it is not made for profit
screens.after: In capitalism the owner of the means of production keeps the profit; workers sell their labour for wages.

screens.title: Five main features
paras: 1. Private ownership of the means of production, especially industry.
2. Two antagonistic classes: capitalists (owners) and workers (wage earners).
3. Capital is reinvested to enlarge production, not spent on pyramids or cathedrals.
4. Companies make and sell goods and services for profit.
5. Laissez-faire: markets work without government intervention.
True capitalists say a free market makes the right supply for demand.
Prices then adjust by themselves.

people.name: Adam Smith
people.did: Economist and moral philosopher; one of the forefathers of capitalism. Wrote "An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations" (1776). Wanted economic decisions left to self-regulating market forces, for the good of business and society.

ideas.name: Karl Marx: the critique of capitalism

en.text: The miserable conditions of 19th-century industrial workers inspired Karl Marx. Marxian economics, the antithesis of capitalism, says the employer exploits the surplus value of the worker's labour, that capitalism suffers systematic crises and concentrates wealth, and that a proletarian-led class war will overthrow it. In socialism the means of production are collective or state-owned and central planning allocates resources.

screens.title: Marx's critique
paras: Industrial capitalism created a vast new class of industrial workers.
Their miserable conditions inspired Karl Marx.
Marxian economics is the antithesis (opposite) of capitalism.
Marx said capitalism segregates capitalists from workers.
Workers sell their labour through wage contracts.
The employer also profits from that labour.
Marx called this exploitation of surplus value.

screens.title: Marx's predictions and plan
paras: Capitalist economies would weaken in systematic crises.
Crises would cause social disturbance.
Wealth would gather in ever fewer, more privileged hands.
A proletarian-led class war would overthrow capitalism.
In socialism there is no private ownership of the means of production.
They are collective or state-owned.
Central planning decides what to produce and how to use resources.

notes.text: p.2: the book defines mercantilism as buying and selling at a higher price for profit, which describes merchant capitalism. The lesson keeps this line and adds the usual meaning (16th–18th c. state policy: favourable balance of trade, bullion, colonies, regulation).

p.3: "They believed that a state could only increase its wealth at the expense of another state" reads as Adam Smith's view; it was the MERCANTILIST belief Smith attacked. The lesson teaches it that way (tf item).
Figure 1.1 caption spells "Fredric Engels"; correct is Friedrich Engels. p.4 "laissez fair" should be laissez-faire.
